summary: Tested transaction edit/delete with balance recomputation against preview backend (local MongoDB, standalone -> non-session path). Backend: 14/14 pytest pass covering PATCH (amount/kasa/client/type/date/description), type-change rules, validation (400/404/422/401), DELETE (client tx, expense + linked expense doc, kasa_transfer, receivable_collection with collected_amount rollback), expense doc sync on edit / type change to/from expense, and POST /api/admin/recalculate-balances (idempotent, matches incremental balances). Frontend: Client detail and Ledger both show Düzenle/Sil per row; edit modal prefilled correctly, Radix selects (type/kasa/expense type) work, save closes modal and list + client-balance refresh without reload; 'Emin misiniz?' dialog cancel keeps row, confirm deletes; Masraflar tab count updates; dashboard kasa cards reflect changes; client-side amount<=0 validation toast works. No bugs found.

issues: Date field uses native <input type=datetime-local> (browser default picker, US mm/dd format in Chromium) instead of shadcn Calendar/Popover - inconsistent with Turkish UI

action_items: Optional: replace native datetime-local in TxEditModal with shadcn date picker (tr locale)

Be aware before production: recompute_balances overwrites ALL kasa/client balances from transaction history; any balance on Render/Atlas not backed by transactions (manual edits, opening balances, legacy drift) will be reset on the first edit/delete. Consider running /admin/recalculate-balances on a copy first or adding an opening-balance transaction type.
critical_code_review_comments: recompute_balances does a full aggregation + bulk_write over all kasalar/clients on every edit/delete - fine for small firms, O(n) per mutation as data grows.
Ledger.load / ClientDetail.refresh have no try/catch or loading/error state; a failed GET after edit leaves stale UI silently.
When type changes expense -> client_to_kasa, stale expense_type remains in tx doc (Ledger shows description||expense_type) - harmless but untidy.
find_linked_expense fallback matches by client/kasa/amount/date for legacy tx without expense_id - could delete wrong doc if two identical expenses exist (edge case).
/api/admin/reset-data and /admin/recalculate-balances are available to any authenticated user (no role check) - consider requiring role=admin.
CORS allow_origins='*' with allow_credentials=True; app uses Bearer tokens so works, but explicit origins recommended.
